canonical_name: python-control -- the Python Control Systems Library
lineage: python-control (2010-, Murray et al., Caltech): LTI systems, state-space and transfer functions, LQR/LQE optimal control, pole placement, frequency response; the open reference implementing the classical/modern control toolbox in Python
version: github.com/python-control/python-control main as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
compiler_or_interpreter: CPython 3.11 + numpy/scipy (docker python:3.11-slim, pip at run time)
entry_points: control.lqr / control.ss / control.forced_response -- design an LQR gain and simulate the closed loop

example.command: Techne harness: build a 2-state plant, design an LQR gain, simulate to the origin from a perturbed state
example.input: a state-space plant + cost matrices Q,R
example.output: the closed-loop state trajectory driven to zero

human_capability_summary.built_to: design and simulate controllers for linear dynamical systems -- compute an optimal state-feedback gain (LQR) that trades control effort against state error, and simulate the resulting closed loop
human_capability_summary.pressure: a multivariable plant with coupled states where hand-tuning fails; the controller must stabilise and optimise a quadratic cost
human_capability_summary.success_means: the closed-loop system is stable and drives the state to the target with the intended effort/error trade-off

known_human_problem_solved: model-based optimal control design (LQR and friends)
human_environmental_pressure: coupled multivariable dynamics, control-effort limits, the effort-vs-error trade-off
human_failure_condition: an unstable or badly-tuned gain lets the state diverge; in a physical plant that is a crash
behavioral_entry_point: change Q/R (cheap vs expensive control), perturb the initial state, or add a disturbance to the simulated plant and watch the LQR response

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run python-control
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: design and simulate controllers for linear dynamical systems -- compute an optimal state-feedback gain (LQR) that trades control effort against state error, and simulate the resulting closed loop
